newsitem.title: UK: Canadian Pacific may carry on Lykes subsidy.
newsitem.headline: Canadian Pacific may carry on Lykes subsidy.

text.p: CP Ships, the division of Canadian Pacific Ltd which has acquired the container shipping operations of Lykes Bros. Steamship Co, said Wednesday it has not given up fighting for U.S. ship operating subsidies.
CP Ships president Ray Miles, who is based in London, told Reuters: "We are disappointed to have lost the subsidies but have not entirely given up on the subject."
Miles was speaking after the company announced it had completed its acquisition of Lykes for $34 million.
The Washington Maritime Administration rejected the continuation of operating subsidies for three U.S. flagged Lykes ships, worth a total $6.3 million, in June.

The subsidies, which are granted for making ships available for military use in times of national emergency, were withdrawn because it was felt the company was coming under "excessive foreign control."

The Marad ruling could have implications for the proposed $825 million merger between APL Ltd and Neptune Orient Lines Ltd. APL has also applied for continued subsidies but said its scheme differs from Lykes.
Miles said: "We have a keen interest in the outcome of the NOL-APL decision and will be looking at that very closely."
"We have not decided how to go forward but we think the ships are suitable and our structure is fine," Miles added.

CP Ships-owned Lykes Lines Limited charters the 2,800 teu ships which were previously eligible for subsidies from Sea Crews ll, a U.S. company owned by former creditors of Lykes Bros - GATX Corp and Gilman.

Miles said Lykes Lines is planning to redeploy its services in order to cut costs but said details have not been finalised. He added that Lykes, which filed for protection under Chapter X1 of U.S. bankruptcy law in 1995, is still losing money.
The company will also rationalise container management, logistics and terminal operations with its owner. -Paul Berrill Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087. Fax 5017.
